headline: Mitsubishi to Expand Ayala Stake in ₱44.5-Billion Philippines Investment
seoTitle: Mitsubishi Expands Ayala Stake in ₱44.5-Billion Deal | FMB News
seoDescription: Mitsubishi Corporation agreed to raise its economic ownership in Ayala Corporation from 4.7% to 15% in a transaction valued at about ₱44.5 billion, subject to closing conditions and regulatory approvals.
deck: The Japanese trading house will increase its economic ownership in Ayala from 4.7% to 15%, deepening a 52-year partnership, if the transaction clears required conditions and approvals.
author: FMB News World Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Mitsubishi Corporation agreed to significantly increase its investment in Ayala Corporation in a transaction valued at approximately ₱44.5 billion. Ayala announced the definitive agreement on September 21, and Reuters independently reported the transaction.

Upon completion, Mitsubishi’s economic ownership in Ayala is expected to rise from 4.7% to 15%, while its voting stake is expected to reach 20%. The transaction combines primary and secondary shares, including a voluntary tender offer.

sections.heading: What is confirmed
paragraphs: Ayala says the agreed subscription and acquisition price is ₱650 per common share. The company expects to receive about ₱20 billion in proceeds, which it says will be used for debt reduction, share purchases and future growth initiatives.
The Philippine Stock Exchange disclosure system records Ayala’s September 21 press release and current report on the transaction.

sections.heading: What remains developing
paragraphs: The transaction has not yet completed. Closing remains subject to conditions precedent, closing conditions and applicable regulatory approvals. Proposed changes to Ayala’s board also depend on required shareholder and regulatory approvals.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: The transaction is a major new Japanese investment in one of the Philippines’ largest diversified conglomerates and deepens economic ties between Japan and the Philippines. Mitsubishi and Ayala have maintained a strategic relationship since 1974 across multiple sectors.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Regulatory and shareholder approvals, the voluntary tender offer and the eventual closing of the transaction will determine when Mitsubishi’s increased ownership becomes effective.
